about.title: Method in brief
about.what: An annual simulation of Belgium to 2070: population, labour market, economy and every revenue and expenditure line of general government. The baseline follows the Federal Planning Bureau to 2031 and the Study Committee on Ageing afterwards; a measure is a change of parameters and its effect is the difference from that baseline.
about.limits_lead: Not an official costing, not a forecast.
about.limits: Results are orders of magnitude. The Validation view shows where the model matches official figures and where it does not; no independent expert has reviewed it yet.

validation.loading: Running the model against the official reference figures…
validation.loading_detail: Every costed measure is simulated twice (with and without behavioural responses). About a minute the first time, then cached until the parameters change.
validation.missing: The server has no validation reference file.
validation.how_text: Each line sets a figure published by an official body next to what the model gives for the same thing. Small gaps on a line close to your question are a reason to trust the result; large gaps say the model answers that kind of question poorly. Confidence is about the reference figure: high = read in the official document, medium = reliable secondary source or simple arithmetic on an official table, low = weaker.
